summary: Montenegro's Decree on Visa Regime (as amended up to Official Gazette 108/26) lets citizens of the countries and territories listed in its Article 1, including the United Kingdom and the United States, visit visa-free for up to 90 days. Citizens of Peru can stay 30 days, and citizens of Belarus, Russia, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye 30 days until 31 October 2026. Holders of a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa, or of a residence permit from those countries or the Schengen area, can enter for up to 30 days.

conditionalWaivers.text: Holders of a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa, or of a residence permit from the Schengen area or one of those countries, may enter Montenegro without a visa and stay up to 30 days, and no longer than until the visa or permit expires if it is valid for less than 30 days. Holders of an APEC Business Travel Card get the same 30 days.

stayDays.text: A short-stay visa (visa C) is issued for the purpose of transit through Montenegro or for the purpose of entering and staying in the territory of Montenegro up to 90 days in a period of 180 days, counting from the day of first entry.

name.text: A short-stay visa (visa C) is issued for one, two or more entries into Montenegro.

method.text: A visa application is submitted to the diplomatic or consular mission in person on the prescribed form.

name.text: A long-stay visa (D visa) is issued to a foreigner who intends to stay in Montenegro for more than 90 days, but not more than 180 days in a period of one year, counting from the date of first entry.

method.text: A visa application is submitted to the diplomatic or consular mission in person on the prescribed form.

passportValidity.text: Montenegro's foreign ministry says a foreign travel document is valid for entry if it was issued within the last ten years and will not expire until at least three months after your planned departure from Montenegro. If you need a visa, the passport must be valid at least three months longer than the visa.

source.name: Government of Montenegro, Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Visas

travelInsurance.text: Montenegro's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists travel health insurance among the requirements for a short-stay (C) visa. No official source we could read states an insurance requirement for visa-exempt visitors.

declarations.text: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors to Montenegro must register with the local tourism office or police within 24 hours of arrival. It says hotel staff and the owners of some holiday lets are obliged to register you; if you stay in private accommodation, make sure you complete the registration yourself. If you do not register, it says, you may be fined, detained or face a court appearance.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises being wary of pickpockets in tourist hot spots, beaches, airports and on public transport and not leaving luggage in a parked vehicle. It says incidents of violent crime between organised criminal groups can affect others close by, and that hikers have got lost in the mountains after leaving marked paths.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors must register with the local tourism office or police within 24 hours of arrival, and that you may be fined, detained or face a court appearance if you do not. If you stay in private accommodation, the UK says to make sure you complete the registration yourself.
The European Central Bank says Montenegro and Kosovo use the euro, but without a formal arrangement.

Under Article 7 of the Decree on Visa Regime, holders of a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa, or of a residence permit from those countries or the Schengen area, can enter Montenegro for up to 30 days, no longer than the visa or permit is valid.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Montenegro?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport: citizens of the countries and territories listed in Article 1 of the Decree on Visa Regime, including the UK, US, Canada, Australia and Japan, can stay up to 90 days visa-free, and Peruvians 30 days. Citizens of Russia, Belarus, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia can stay 30 days, an exemption the decree sets only until 31 October 2026. Nationalities that do need a visa can apply in person at a Montenegrin diplomatic or consular mission, or enter on a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa or a residence permit from those countries or the Schengen area for up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can I enter Montenegro with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes — under Article 7 of the Decree on Visa Regime, holders of a valid Schengen visa or a Schengen-area residence permit (and equally of US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visas and residence permits) may enter and stay up to 30 days without a Montenegrin visa, and no longer than until the visa or permit expires if it is valid for less than 30 days.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Montenegro?
faq.answer: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days without a visa, under Montenegro's Decree on Visa Regime.

faq.question: Does Montenegro use the euro?
faq.answer: Yes. The European Central Bank says Montenegro uses the euro, but without a formal arrangement.

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Montenegro?
faq.answer: Not until 31 October 2026: Montenegro's Decree on Visa Regime lets Russian citizens enter visa-free for up to 30 days, and sets that exemption only until that date.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter Montenegro with just an ID card?
faq.answer: Yes — Montenegro's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says EU citizens can stay up to 30 days with a valid ID card and up to 90 days with a valid passport, and that citizens of the signatory states of the Agreement on Freedom of Movement in the Western Balkans can enter and stay for up to 90 days with a valid personal document.

We also note that citizens of the signatory states of the Agreement on Freedom of Movement in the Western Balkans can enter, transit through the territory and stay in Montenegro for up to 90 days without a visa, with a valid personal document issued by the competent authority.
